EX-99.1 2 abos-20261030xexx991.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 Acumen Pharmaceuticals Announces Topline Results from Phase 2 ALTITUDE-AD Clinical Trial of Sabirnetug (ACU193) for the Treatment of Early Alzheimer’s Disease; Trial Did Not Meet Primary Endpoint -- Topline data show that ALTITUDE-AD did not meet the primary endpoint of change from baseline in cognitive and functional decline as measured by the Integrated Alzheimer’s Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) at 18 months compared to placebo at either dose; key secondary endpoints, including CDR-SB, also did not achieve statistical significance -- -- Acumen to cease clinical development of sabirnetug, preserve cash and explore strategic options -- NEWTON, MA, Oct. 30, 2026 – Acumen Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

(NASDAQ: ABOS) (“Acumen” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapeutics that target toxic soluble amyloid beta oligomers (AβOs) for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), today announced that initial topline data from its Phase 2 ALTITUDE-AD clinical trial of sabirnetug (ACU193) in participants with early AD did not meet its primary endpoint of change from baseline in cognitive and functional decline as measured by the Integrated Alzheimer’s Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) at 18 months compared to placebo at either the 35 mg/kg or the 50 mg/kg dose.

Based on the initial topline results, Acumen plans to cease development of sabirnetug, including the open-label extension portion of the ALTITUDE-AD trial, and to evaluate its strategic options, including its Enhanced Brain Delivery™ (EBD®) program.

These statements are based upon the current beliefs and expectations of Acumen’s management, and are subject to certain factors, risks and uncertainties, including the risk that additional data or further analyses from ALTITUDE-AD may differ from, or change the interpretation of, the topline results, and particularly those inherent in the process of discovering, developing and commercializing safe and effective human therapeutics.
